(1) dermoscopic patterns of regression and involution of melanocytic nevi are different from each other and (2) dermoscopes can be useful in following the natural course of melanocytic lesions.
the dermoscopic changes in nevi that are undergoing involution are distinct and can be classified as regression and halo.
dermoscopy provides insights into understanding distinct pathways to nevogenesis.

the development and application of new methods for the analysis of the dynamics of complex systems.
the development, implementation, evaluation, and dissemination of a model of care for patients with skin disease in primary care.
the study of the mechanisms underlying the formation and evolution of melanocytic nevi.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nevi are benign lesions, but they can undergo malignant transformation, and therefore, they should be considered as a risk factor for the development of melanoma.
the dermoscopic patterns of nevi are dynamic and can change with time.
melanocytic nevi can be expected to involute, with the exception of congenital nevi, which may persist throughout life, and atypical nevi, which are at risk of malignant transformation.

the most important factor for a patient to be able to achieve a good result in the treatment of a nevus would be the patient’s motivation and compliance.
